With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Coquitlam East

items.t: Established east-side house lots: single-detached streets under the City's small-scale residential zones R-1, R-2 and R-3 (Zoning Bylaw No. 3000, 1996), with a much thinner strata segment than the city average. A fee-simple lot carries NO strata, NO Form B and NO strata fees.

Lot character from the zones, as the City states it: minimum lot size for subdivision is 650 m² with 18.5 m width for R-1 and R-3, and 465 m² with 12.5 m width for R-2; the SSMUH unit counts turn on the 280 m² and 4,050 m² thresholds. These are zone minimums, not a claim about any existing lot's size — the zone and dimensions of a specific lot are confirmed parcel by parcel: Not verified for any individual lot.

Serviced position, as the City states it: Coquitlam's SSMUH framework expressly leaves lots not connected to municipal water or sewer OUTSIDE the SSMUH rules — the City's own servicing qualifier for house lots here — and Coquitlam utility charges cover water, sewer and drainage and solid waste. Property-level septic or well status is not verified: confirm servicing for the specific lot with the City before pricing in added units.

Watercourse character — the 50-metre Northeast rule: the Watercourse Protection Development Permit Area covers all areas within 50 metres of the top of bank of any watercourse in Northeast Coquitlam, and within 30 metres in the rest of Coquitlam — which side of that line a Coquitlam East lot sits on is a parcel check, and creek- and ravine-edge lots carry permit diligence.

ALR vs non-ALR: ALR status for the sub-area is not verified; no ALR parcel and no ALR percentage split is confirmed. ALR status is a property-specific check in the Agricultural Land Commission's ALR Property and Map Finder.

Market context, labelled correctly: Coquitlam IS a SnapStats-covered community; SnapStats has NO land category. September 2026 context only, never land figures: Coquitlam East sub-area detached inventory 28 / solds 4 (14%) and "Condos & Townhomes" combined 9 / 1 (11%); Coquitlam community detached median $1,455,000 and "Condos & Townhomes" combined median $625,000. Sub-area medians are not verified (community level only).
No bare-land strata plan in Coquitlam East was verified

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Coquitlam East

items.t: Coquitlam East is the established east side of the City of Coquitlam, around David Avenue, Coast Meridian Road and the Eagle Ridge / Lansdowne Drive slopes below Burke Mountain. "Coquitlam East" is the GVR sub-area name as it appears in the SnapStats GVR September 2026 report; the City planning areas on the east side include Ranch Park and the Northeast Coquitlam area, and an exact official planning-area match for "Coquitlam East" was not confirmed. Boundaries: NOT CONFIRMED — no City neighbourhood plan boundary for Coquitlam East is stated on a City page in the sources read: Not verified.
Main roads: Lougheed Highway, David Avenue and Coast Meridian Road serve east Coquitlam; exact sub-area boundary roads: Not verified.

Nearby areas: Central Coquitlam to the west, Burke Mountain / Northeast Coquitlam (Hyde Creek, Smiling Creek, Partington Creek) to the north-east, Port Coquitlam across the Coquitlam River to the east, and Port Moody to the west.

Transit: Coquitlam Central Station (Millennium Line Evergreen Extension and West Coast Express), at Lougheed Highway and Pinetree Way, is the main station for east Coquitlam; per-route bus numbers for the sub-area's interior streets: Not verified. Commute times in minutes: Not verified.

blocks.text: Good to know about Coquitlam East

items.t: A search filtered to one sub-area name alone silently drops the other half of the slope's stock.

The watercourse setback doubles at an invisible line: 50 metres from the top of bank in Northeast Coquitlam versus 30 metres in the rest of the city — two otherwise similar east-side lots can carry materially different buildable envelopes purely on which side of the Northeast Coquitlam line they sit, and no City plan boundary for "Coquitlam East" itself is published to settle it from the street.

A "Not allowed" rental line from 2019 is void law today: the 455 Bromley Street feature sheet's "Pet/Rental: Not allowed" line predates November 24, 2022, when every BC strata long-term rental-restriction bylaw became void — the pet half remains not confirmed against the registered bylaws, but no buyer should price the rental half as a live restriction.

faq.a: No verified one — no named bare-land subdivision, bare-land strata plan or presale lot offering was verified. Land trades as built house lots on the east-side streets and the thin Atlin Place / Bromley strata segment.
faq.q: Is there a vacant lot subdivision I can buy into in Coquitlam East?

faq.a: Yes under the City's SSMUH rules — up to 3 units on lots 280 m² or smaller and up to 4 units on lots larger than 280 m² and under 4,050 m², including secondary suites and carriage / laneway homes — but lots not connected to municipal water or sewer fall outside the rules, so confirm services and the exact zone (R-1 / R-2 / R-3) before advertising unit potential.
faq.q: Can a Coquitlam East house lot add units?

faq.a: Search both sub-area names or you will miss listings either way.
faq.q: Are the Lansdowne Drive townhomes Coquitlam East or Eagle Ridge?

faq.a: The City's framework assumes municipal water and sewer for SSMUH eligibility and bills water, sewer/drainage and solid waste as City utilities — but parcel-level septic or well status is not verified, so confirm servicing for the specific lot with the City before writing.
faq.q: Is a Coquitlam East lot serviced?

faq.a: The Subdivision and Development Servicing Bylaw No. 3558, 2003 — works and services to the City's standards under that bylaw, including owner-granted statutory rights-of-way and owner-paid City signage, confirmed parcel by parcel with the City.
faq.q: What servicing bylaw governs a subdivision here?

faq.a: Coquitlam Central Station (Millennium Line, Evergreen Extension) is the main station for east Coquitlam, and it also has West Coast Express service.
